title: Implement Array.prototype.myMap and myFilter
subtopicTitle: Core Array & Utility Polyfills from Scratch
problemStatement: Implement `myMap(callback, thisArg)` and `myFilter(callback, thisArg)` on `Array.prototype`. They must correctly skip empty slots (sparse arrays) and pass `(element, index, array)` to the callback.
interviewTrap: Using simple `for` loop without `if (i in this)` visits empty array holes and converts them to `undefined`, violating the spec.

myMap preserves sparse array holes

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Native array methods must respect sparse arrays (`in` operator check), handle absent `initialValue` in `reduce` (skipping holes to find the first real element), and preserve the caller's prototype chain.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Array Iteration & Sparse Index Handling.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Array Iteration & Sparse Index Handling is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: Using simple `for` loop without `if (i in this)` visits empty array holes and converts them to `undefined`, violating the spec.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How do Array.prototype.myMap and myFilter handle sparse arrays (holes)?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Per ECMA-262 §23.1.3.14, `map` and `filter` must inspect whether the index is an 'own property' using `k in array` (or `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(array, k)`). If an array is sparse (e.g. `[1, , 3]`), index 1 is a hole; the callback MUST NOT be invoked for index 1, and the resulting array must preserve the hole for `map`.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: The #1 trap question when implementing array polyfills.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What should map and filter do if thisArg is provided?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: The callback must be invoked using `callback.call(thisArg, array[k], k, array)` so that any `this` references inside the callback point to the passed `thisArg`.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Checks complete adherence to the standard API signature.

realWorldUseCases.description: Transforming backend API arrays into normalized entity maps or filtered UI view collections.

howToExplain.opening: Specification-compliant map and filter polyfills iterate over elements while strictly respecting sparse array holes and thisArg binding.
keyPoints: Checks 'k in array' before invoking the callback to skip holes in sparse arrays.
Passes element, index, and original array to callback.
Creates a fresh array without mutating the source.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Respecting sparse array holes is what distinguishes an amateur polyfill from a specification-grade implementation.
analogies: Walking down a street: if a house number is an empty lot (hole), the mail carrier skips it without trying to deliver a letter.

commonMistakes.mistake: Checking array[k] !== undefined instead of k in array.
commonMistakes.why: An array can contain an explicit `undefined` element `[undefined]`, which is NOT a hole and MUST be processed.
commonMistakes.correct: Use `k in array` to test for slot existence.

followUpDeepDive.question: What is an exotic Array object in ECMA-262?
followUpDeepDive.answer: An exotic Array object has a customized internal `[[DefineOwnProperty]]` method that automatically updates the `.length` property when numeric indices are added, and truncates elements when `.length` is decreased.
